title: How AI answers from your documents

cues.title: Your documents. A useful answer.
cues.text: Ever wondered how an AI assistant can answer questions about your own documents?

cues.title: Start with a real question.
cues.text: Let's say you ask, "What's our refund policy?"

cues.title: Find the relevant passages.
cues.text: First, it searches your documents and pulls out the passages that seem most relevant.

cues.title: Give the model evidence.
cues.text: It sends those passages, along with your question, to a language model.

cues.title: Draft an answer with a source.
cues.text: The model uses that context to draft an answer, with a source you can check.

cues.title: Review before you act.
cues.text: You review the source before deciding what to do.

cues.title: Retrieval + generation = RAG.
cues.text: That approach is called retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG.

cues.title: Helpful context. Still worth checking.
cues.text: It makes answers easier to check. But the documents, or the answer itself, can still be wrong.
